title: Consumers: social media, CMS communications and Brand Effect
summary: The first consumer is CMS as a communications system, not a content ownership or publishing truth store. Media inputs may come from social media and other source-service adapters. Librarian supplies provenance-qualified, time-scoped claims, stance and selection evidence; downstream Brand Interaction Effect/Brand Journey and Reputation Effect assess their distinct impacts. Structured Utterance and Intentions are candidate providers for communicative purpose and meaning, with contracts verified before binding.
invariants: Keep ingestion connectors separate from the semantic/evidence core.
Transport-independent semantic service; direct ooRexx, RPC or Queue Fabric are adapter choices, not compulsory dependencies.
Brand effects are not bias judgments; editorial framing is not automatically factual error.
CMS communication proposals, publication and interventions remain authorised downstream; observation must not cause action.
Do not invent a binding to ongoing Intentions or NLP similarity implementations without checking exact API packages.

provenance.claim: Observed comparative positioning records and source/origin identifiers.
